title: Measuring the Spin-Lattice Relaxation Magnetic Field Dependence of Hyperpolarized [1-13C]pyruvate
protocol: Prepare 1 mL of stock 13C-enriched pyruvic acid solution consisting of 15-mmol/L triarylmethyl radical dissolved in [1-13C]pyruvic acid.
Click on the Cooldown button to lower the temperature of the variable temperature insert (VTI) to 1.4 K.
Load 10 µL of the stock solution into a sample cup once the DNP has reached the desired temperature.
Open the turret doors and insert the cup into the VTI using an insertion wand designed for this task.
Quickly extract the wand and ensure the cup is released.
Close the turret doors after inserting the sample.
Prepare the DNP to run a microwave sweep in order to find the optimal RF frequency for hyperpolarization of the stock solution.
Establish communication between the spectrometer and DNP control software using HyperTerminal with appropriate serial parameters.
Launch RINMR software and type .HYPERSENSEMNR in its command line.
Press enter after typing the command.
Type number one (1) in the Configuration Number field of the new window that appears.
Click on the Select Configuration button.
Click on the Do microwave sweep button to initiate a small window with a descending counter of seconds indicating readiness for periodic trigger signals.
On the DNP control software, select the Calibrate tab and click on the Generate button.
Enter Start Frequency = 94.117 GHz in the calibration setup window.
Enter End Frequency = 94.137 GHz in the calibration setup window.
Enter Step Size = 1 MHz in the calibration setup window.
Enter Step Duration = 300 s in the calibration setup window.
Enter Power = 50 mW in the calibration setup window.
Enter Liquid Helium Level = 65% in the calibration setup window.
Enter Temperature = 1.4 K in the calibration setup window.
Click on the Generate button to close the setup window and return to the Calibrate tab displaying steps and time for microwave sweep.
Once the desired VTI temperature is achieved, click the Enable button.
Click Start to initialize the microwave sweep process.
Recover the sample at the end of the microwave sweep.
Record the optimal frequency where maximum polarization is achieved.
Prepare 250 mL of stock dissolution medium using a solution of 40-mmol/L Tris base, 50 mmol/L sodium chloride, and 80-mmol/L sodium hydroxide in de-ionized water.
Add EDTA at a concentration of 100 mg/L to the dissolution medium.
Prepare 500 mL of stock cleaning solution consisting of 100 mg/L EDTA dissolved in deionized water.
Cool the DNP apparatus to 1.4 K by pressing the Cooldown button in the DNP main window.
Proceed with the following steps if the software used for the spectrometer is already active with configuration 1 selected.
Otherwise, perform steps 1.5.1 to 1.5.3 and then continue with the following steps.
Verify that configuration 1 is selected in the window controlling the DNP's spectrometer.
Click on the Solid Build Up button.
Enter the file name SSBuilupXXX where "XXX" is a number incremented by the software.
Click OK.
Weigh out 30 mg of pyruvic acid - OX063 stock solution in a sample cup.
When the desired VTI temperature (1.4 K) is achieved, click on Insert Sample.
Select Normal Sample and then click on Next.
Following safety precautions displayed on the screen, insert the cup into the cold DNP apparatus using a long wand designed for this task.
Once the cup is inserted and the wand removed, close the DNP doors.
Click Next and then Finish.
At that point, the hyperpolarizer system lowers the sample cup to the irradiation chamber partially filled (65%) with liquid helium.
Wait until the temperature has returned to 1.4K.
Click on the Polarize Sample button.
Set the frequency value in the new pop up window to that obtained from the microwave sweep in step 1.6.
Set the power to 50 mW and the sampling time to 300 s in the same window.
Click on Next, check the Enable Build-up Monitoring box.
Click on Finish.
Monitor the polarization build-up curve generated by the spectrometer software.
Fit the curve to an exponential growth function after the 4th sample and every subsequent sample.
Calculate the percentage polarization achieved based on the fitted parameters.
Polarize until the solid-state magnetization reaches at least 95% of maximum.
Prepare the Fast-Field-Cycling Relaxometer as explained in Section 2.
Click on Run Dissolution and under Method, select Pyruvic Acid Test.
Open the DNP turret doors.
Load the heating and pressurizing chamber with ~4.55 mL of the dissolution medium to produce an 80-mmol/L pyruvate concentration upon dissolution at a pH of ~7.75 and temperature of ~37 °C.
Position the recovering wand in the right position, close the turret doors.
Click on Next and then on Finish at the computer.
Swirl the pear-shaped flask constantly as the hyperpolarized pyruvate/dissolution media mixture is ejected through a capillary tubing into it.
Draw 1.1 mL of the liquid into a syringe once all the mixture has been ejected.
Transfer the drawn liquid to a pre-warmed (37 °C) 10-mm-diameter NMR tube.
Rapidly transport the NMR tube to the field-cycling relaxometer.
Dispense remaining aliquot of every pyruvate dissolution into a 0.55-T benchtop NMR spectrometer.
Immediately clean DNP fluid path using clean dissolution medium followed by ethanol.
Blow helium gas through fluid path to remove remaining cleaning fluids and purge path of oxygen.
Clean all glassware.
Record the pH of samples from both the bench top spectrometer and the field-cycling relaxometer after each measurement.
Weigh all agents and solvents with a precision of 0.1 mg for accurate preparation of final hyperpolarized solutions.
Prepare 1 mL of neat [1-13C]pyruvic acid in an NMR tube.
Add gadolinium contrast agent to reduce the T1 of the 13C nuclei to less than 200 ms but more than 50 ms.
Seal the NMR tube for use as a calibration standard.
Set the depth of insertion of the NMR tube using the relaxometer's depth gauge.
Mark the insertion depth with adhesive tape for repeatability.
Place the depth stopper on the NMR tube as indicated by the tape.
Insert the calibration standard into the bore of the field-cycling relaxometer and secure it with a weight.
Set the temperature controller to 37°C using heated air from the instrument air valve.
Install and energize the external shim coil.
Tune and match the RF coil to 8 MHz (~0.75 T for 13C nuclei).
Use the appropriate λ/4 cable for signal acquisition.
Select the Main par tab in the instrument software.
Scroll down in the pop-up window to select "13CANGLE.FFC" pulse sequence under Experiment.
Set RFA = 5; SWT = 0.005, RD = 0.5, BPOL = 30 MHz, TPOL = 0.5.
Select the Acq. par tab and then the Basic sub-tab in the instrument software.
Scroll down to select 13C under Nucleus in the pop-up window.
Set SF = 8 MHz.
Set BS = 652.
Set FLTR = 100000.
Set MS = 32.
Select Conf sub-tab.
Set RINH = 25.
Set ACQD = 25.
Select nDim sub-tab.
Set NBLK = 32.
Set BINI = 2.
Set BEND = 62.
Select Evaluation tab and then Parameters sub-tab.
Set EWIP = 10.
Set EWEP = 128.
Set EWIB = 1.
Set EWEB = 32.
Click Start Acquisition icon to run the pulse sequence.
Save the data after acquisition is finished.
Select Evaluation dialog icon.
From analysis menu select WAM Window: Absolute Magnitude.
Select Report Sheet, Graphs and Export File.
Click on Execute.
Find the RF pulse width that provides the maximum amplitude in the Report window.
Fine-tune the value with the help of the cursor in the displayed graph.
Adjust the frequency shift of the relaxometer by clicking the F1 icon.
Select HPUB/S pulse sequence from the pop-up window.
Set RFA = 25 and T1MX values between 3 and 5.
Set SWT = 0.2, RD = 0, BRLX to desired relaxation field in MHz.
Scroll down to Nucleus sub-tab and select 13C.
Set SF = 8 MHz, SW = 1000000, BS = 652, FLTR = 50000.
Go to Conf sub-tab, set PW90 as value from step 2.1.10, RINH = 25, ACQD = 25.
Set PW = 5 under Puls sub-tab.
Set NBLK = 100 under nDim sub-tab.
Wait and receive the hyperpolarized solution to start data acquisition.
Manually initiate pulse sequence from console before inserting sample.
Ignore first Free Induction Decay (FID) during data analysis.
Save acquired data by clicking Save button.
Integrate magnitude of each FID signal using analysis software.
Produce a data series with sample magnetization as function of time.
Extract the spin-lattice relaxation time from a three-parameter exponential model using a standard non-linear least-squares fitting algorithm implemented in commercial analytical software.
Assume even weighting for all data points during analysis.
